question: Can accumulated karma make the self a real agent rather than a figurative one?
premises: An opponent may say the self is the sharer of accumulated actions.
Calling the self a sharer of action can still be only figurative.
A figurative attribution does not establish real agency.
inference: Therefore, appeal to accumulated karma does not overcome the charge of figurative agency.
plain_english: If one says the self is the sharer of accumulated actions, that too would be only figurative usage — and that has already been shown to be inadequate.
